source.author: lucan
source.text: Sed dira satelles Regis dona ferens, medium provectus in aequor, Colla gerit Magni, Phario velamine tecta, Ac prius infanda commendat crimina voce: Terrarum domitor, Romanae maxime gentis, Et, quod adhuc nescis, genero secure perempto; Rex tibi Pellaeus terrae pelagique labores Donat et , Emathiis quod solum defuit armis, Exhibet: absenti bellum civile peractum est.
source.text_original: Sed dira satelles / Regis dona ferens, medium provectus in aequor, / Colla gerit Magni, Phario velamine tecta, / Ac prius infanda commendat crimina voce: / Terrarum domitor, Romanae maxime gentis, / Et, quod adhuc nescis, genero secure perempto; / Rex tibi Pellaeus terrae pelagique labores / Donat et , Emathiis quod solum defuit armis, / Exhibet: absenti bellum civile peractum est.
source.text_english:
But the dreadful attendant of the king, bearing gifts, advanced into the middle of the sea, carrying the head of Magnus, covered with a Pharian veil, and first with hateful speech he recommends his crimes:

Conqueror of lands, greatest of the Roman people, and, what you do not yet know, since your son-in-law has been safely slain; the Pellaean king grants you the labors of land and sea, and presents what alone was lacking to the Emathian arms: the civil war has been brought to an end in your absence.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: securus in aequor haut minus Erginus, proles Neptunia, fertur, qui maris insidias, clarae qui sidera noctis norit et e clausis quem destinet Aeolus antris, non metuat cui regna ratis, cui tradere caelum assidua Tiphys vultum lassatus ab Arcto.
reuse.text_original: securus in aequor / haut minus Erginus, proles Neptunia, fertur, / qui maris insidias, clarae qui sidera noctis / norit et e clausis quem destinet Aeolus antris, / non metuat cui regna ratis, cui tradere caelum / assidua Tiphys vultum lassatus ab Arcto.
reuse.text_english: Secure, into the sea is borne Erginus, no less so, a child of Neptune, one who knows the sea’s ambushes, one who knows the stars of the clear night and whom Aeolus dispatches from his closed caves, who need not fear the ship’s dominion, to whom Tiphys, worn out by constant watch, wishes to entrust the sky, steering from the North.
